profile.headline: Lead Ground & Mission Control Software Developer at Millennium Space Systems
profile.jobTitle: Lead Ground & Mission Control Software Developer
profile.summary:
From my first experience dragging blocks across a screen for a robotics class, to writing a Python script that filled out my end-of-shift forms for me, the ability to create anything imaginable from only numbers and letters (only 0;s and 1's if we're being technical) has never ceased to inspire me. From the moment I witnessed a Lego robot fight another Lego robot using code I wrote, I knew writing software was the only thing I could ever want to do. After high school, I obtained my B.S. in Computer Science from Auburn University, growing more and more certain of my choice with each test and assignment.

Now, working as a real time embedded software engineer allows me to see my code interact with the world. Each day brings new unique intellectual challenges that I look forward to solving together with my team. 

When I'm not at work, you can find me writing, playing board games with friends, or playing piano. 

I look forward to connecting with you!

positions.title: Lead Ground & Mission Control Software Developer
Resident Assistant
positions.description: As an on-campus Resident Assistant, I planned and implemented community-building activities every month for over 100 residents. Likewise, I counseled and advised these students on academic and personal issues in order to help them succeed in their time at college.

positions.title: Engineering Student Tutor
positions.description: As an Engineering Student Tutor, I worked with 1-5 students a week who are struggling in a variety of academic topics, from chemistry to mathematics to computer science. While I aided them with breaking down content-based questions into understandable terms, I also aimed to communicate to them the process of developing strong study skills so that they may succeed in their majors.

company.name: Auburn University, Samuel Ginn College of Engineering

positions.title: Commercialization Intern
positions.description: As a Commercialization Intern, my time was split between conducting prior art searches and marketing technologies to companies. These tasks require gaining an in-depth knowledge of a variety of academic fields, prompting me to become proficient in comprehending research papers and technical patents. This position enabled me to bridge the gap between the technical and business worlds, gaining skills such as analyzing commercial markets as well as conducting research to assess the patentability of university technologies.

company.name: Auburn University Office of Innovation Advancement & Commercialization (IAC)

positions.title: Camp Counselor
positions.description: As a Camp Counselor, I led and supervised around 15-50 middle and high school aged students each week in various academic camps. I did this with a rotating team of around 2-4 other counselors, adapting to the working styles of each set of counselors and collaborating with them in order to maintain a safe, fun, and educational environment for the campers.

company.name: Auburn University Office of Professional and Continuing Education
